messages:
mira: Hey - Customer GOSSET hitting consistent 429s from Dedicated pool despite healthy node metrics. Started ~08:17 UTC, ~10% of requests failing. Sample curl and headers below. Anyone seen this pattern?

mira: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 14 May 2024 08:19:02 GMT
X-RateLimit-Tenant: tenant_gosset
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1684065542
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "message": "per-tenant capacity limit reached"
}
```

carla: Receiving the escalation. Was notified by CS at 08:21. Customer says they did a burst import of documents last night, but Dedicated pool has spare GPU headroom.

jason: Can you paste the tenant config for GOSSET (rate profile + quota) and which Dedicated pool they're on?

mira: Pool: rwd-dedicated-eu-1, pool usage shows 40% GPU util. Tenant profile snippet (from billing DB):

mira: ```
tenant_id: tenant_gosset
rate_units: 60000
rate_unit_type: minutes
burst_cap: 1200
allocated_pool: rwd-dedicated-eu-1
```

lenore: Hmm that rate_unit_type looks suspicious. We normally store per-minute units as `units_per_minute` but quota service reads `rate_unit_type` expecting `seconds` or `minutes` and then multiplies by denom. If somebody set a raw value in minutes but the mapping was applied twice it could shrink effective units.

samir: I pulled the rate-limit logs. The rate-limiter served 429s because tenant_quota_tokens went to zero repeatedly. Rule applied: `quota_key: tenant_gosset:global` with denom_multiplier = 60 in runtime mapping. But the stored profile already had minutes baked in. Looks like a double-multiplier.

ops-bot: autoscale-event: pool=rwd-dedicated-eu-1, scale_capacity=+0, reason=policy_min, timestamp=1684065560

jason: So autoscaler didn't kick because nodes not saturated. This is purely logical quota exhaustion per-tenant. Can we repro locally by hitting the tenant key with same header?

mira: Repro script I ran (10 clients x burst):

mira: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-gosset" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

mira: After ~90 requests we start seeing 429s.

carla: Customer claim: they had been on a plan migration yesterday. Could be a conversion bug. Assigning root cause triage. @jason @lenore please own.

lenore: I'm checking the migration job logs - found a conversion script that converts `rate_units` for legacy tenants: it multiplies by 60 to go from minutes->seconds, but an earlier codepath already normalized some tenants. GOSSET went through both.

samir: Confirmed: tenant_gosset stored value = 60000 (we thought it was units/min), runtime mapping multiplies by 1 (expected), but legacy migration also multiplied by 60. Effective quota became 36,000,000 -> Wait no, the math: original intended 60k/min, migration mistakenly set to 60k*60 -> 3.6M per minute? That would be higher, not lower.

jason: Maybe the bug is inverse: someone accidentally set denom to hours in the runtime (units_per_hour) so system divides by 60 lowering allowance. Check the quota-service feature flags.

support-bot: config-change: quota-service/feature/legacy-migration-mode toggled OFF by lenore at 08:33 UTC

lenore: Found the actual bug: when we read `rate_unit_type=minutes` we apply denom_multiplier=60 for internal token rate (tokens/sec). But after migration we also set `internal_rate` field. At read time, code used `if internal_rate: use internal_rate` else `compute(internal_rate)`. For GOSSET internal_rate was null due to a failed previous write. Then code erroneously applied both branches due to a race, writing an internal_rate that was 1/60th of expected. TL;DR: effective per-second allowance was 1/60th of what billing UI showed.

carla: Nice catch. Does a hotfix exist?

samir: I pushed a guarded change to quota-service that prefers persisted internal_rate if present and fixes race. Rolling to prod with canary to 10% now. `deploy id=deploy-rl-quota-20240514-hotfix`

ops-bot: deploy-notice: deploy-rl-quota-20240514-hotfix -> rwd-quota-svc (canary 10%) at 08:40 UTC

mira: After canary we flipped 100% at 08:45. Customer reports errors dropped to near zero at 08:49.

carla: Customer notified and asked for postmortem. What do we recommend to prevent this for migrated tenants?

lenore: Action items: 1) Backfill internal_rate for all legacy tenants where null (db job queued: job_id=backfill-1684065900). 2) Add integration test for migration path and race condition. 3) Add alert when tenant effective_rate deviates >20% from UI-exposed rate.

jason: I'll follow up with CS to offer credits; ask GOSSET if they'd like assistance re-running their import at a throttled rate.

carla: Great. Closing thread after postmortem. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

mira: Marking resolved on our side — monitoring for 1hr.
